campaignScope: n=1 case study; not a general performance estimate

fixedPrompts.title: Pune historical rainfall
fixedPrompts.text: For the Pune district polygon, return annual rainfall for every calendar year from 2000 through 2020 inclusive, in mm/year, with one row per year. Using the finite annual values, calculate the arithmetic mean, identify all tied wettest and driest years, and fit an ordinary least-squares trend with year as the predictor, reporting the slope in both mm/year and mm/decade. State the data source, spatial aggregation method, and missing-data behavior. Include a labelled chart, the full table, and an export containing the reported values and provenance.

oracle.intent: Historical annual rainfall time series and reproducible summary for the Pune district polygon.
requiredOutputs: 21 calendar-year rows unless missing years are explicitly represented
OLS slope in mm/year and mm/decade
oracle.semantics: Calendar years 2000-2020 inclusive; arithmetic mean over finite annual values; OLS(value ~ intercept + year); decade slope is 10 times annual slope.
referenceChecks: mean equals finite-value sum divided by finite count
acceptableAlternatives: Area-weighted grid-cell aggregation or zonal aggregation when disclosed and source-consistent
oracle.independentVerification: available only when a registered reference worksheet covers the same source and aggregation

fixedPrompts.title: Pune rainfall follow-up
fixedPrompts.text: Using exactly the dataset and definitions from the previous Pune rainfall answer, calculate the absolute wettest-minus-driest difference and its percentage relative to the driest finite value. Then recompute the arithmetic mean and ordinary least-squares trend for 2005 through 2020 inclusive. Show the arithmetic, disclose whether you reused prior results or retrieved data again, and identify every assumption that changed; do not silently change the source, polygon, units, annual aggregation, or missing-data treatment.

oracle.intent: Test follow-up memory and derived calculations without definition drift.
oracle.semantics: Difference = max - min; percent = difference / min * 100 when min is finite and non-zero; subset years 2005-2020 inclusive.
referenceChecks: derived values agree with P01 returned rows
decade slope conversion is exact before rounding
acceptableAlternatives: Refusal to calculate percentage if the driest value is zero, with explanation

fixedPrompts.title: Ahmedabad projections
fixedPrompts.text: For Ahmedabad district, compare annual mean temperature and annual hot-day count under CRAVIS-native RCP 4.5 and RCP 8.5 for every available future window through 2070. Define the hot-day threshold, reference baseline, ensemble treatment, units, downscaling, bias correction, and uncertainty. Return scenario-by-window values in a table and visualise both metrics without implying that RCP 4.5/8.5 are interchangeable with SSP scenarios.

oracle.intent: Projection comparison across native CRAVIS scenarios and windows.
requiredOutputs: all available future windows ending by 2070
oracle.semantics: Use CRAVIS-native scenario labels and available windows; do not map RCP to IRT SSP contracts without source support.
referenceChecks: all returned windows are future windows through 2070
hot-day counts fall within disclosed annual-calendar bounds
acceptableAlternatives: Different documented hot-day thresholds when the product exposes more than one definition

fixedPrompts.title: Projection follow-up
fixedPrompts.text: Using the values returned in the previous Ahmedabad projection answer without changing any definitions, find the window and metric with the largest absolute RCP 8.5 minus RCP 4.5 difference. Show the arithmetic for every candidate difference, explain whether the reported uncertainty supports identifying a largest difference, and return the underlying scenario-by-window rows in machine-readable form. If the values or uncertainty are insufficient, say so rather than retrieving or inventing replacements.

oracle.intent: Test memory, comparison arithmetic, uncertainty reasoning, and machine-readable output.
oracle.semantics: Within-metric differences only; absolute magnitude determines the maximum; uncertainty may make ranking non-identifiable.
referenceChecks: no cross-unit comparison unless normalized method is explicitly justified
acceptableAlternatives: Separate largest difference per metric because metric units are incompatible
unsupportedClaimTraps: claiming significance from overlapping uncertainty without a test

fixedPrompts.title: Uttarakhand landslides
fixedPrompts.text: Rank all available Uttarakhand districts by the count of unique recorded landslide events over CRAVIS's full declared observation period. Return the top ten and every tie affecting the tenth rank, plus a map and full ranking table. State the event source and period, the event deduplication rule, how events are assigned to district boundaries, and how missing coordinates are handled.

oracle.intent: Spatial event deduplication, district assignment, ranking, and tie handling.
oracle.semantics: Rank descending by unique event count over the product's full declared period; include all ties at rank ten.
acceptableAlternatives: Explicitly documented boundary version and point-on-boundary convention

fixedPrompts.title: Odisha cyclone and rainfall
fixedPrompts.text: Identify the Odisha district with the shortest declared cyclone return period, then return that district's annual rainfall and monsoon rainfall for each year from 2014 through 2024 inclusive. Define return period, name the cyclone-event source, explain the temporal join and rainfall spatial/temporal aggregation, represent missing years explicitly, and keep statistical association separate from any causal claim.

oracle.intent: Cross-dataset selection and time-series join without causal overclaim.
oracle.semantics: Use declared cyclone return period for selection; retain all eleven requested calendar years in output or explicitly mark absent data.
referenceChecks: annual rainfall is not less than same-year monsoon rainfall absent disclosed incompatible products
acceptableAlternatives: Product-native monsoon definition if dates/months are disclosed
unsupportedClaimTraps: return period treated as deterministic schedule

fixedPrompts.title: Heat and healthcare intersection
fixedPrompts.text: Among districts for which compatible data are available, filter to districts with a positive historical hot-day trend and rank them by the lowest number of healthcare facilities per 100,000 people. State the historical heat window and hot-day threshold, the population denominator year/source, exact join keys, and the component values used for each ranked district. If the population denominator needed for a per-100,000 rate is unavailable, do not invent or substitute a different denominator.

oracle.intent: Governed multi-source intersection with explicit denominators and joins.
oracle.semantics: Inner compatible-data population must be disclosed; rate = facilities / population * 100000 using a valid aligned denominator.
referenceChecks: all included trends are strictly positive
rates recompute from shown facility and population values
acceptableAlternatives: Refusal/narrowing when no compatible denominator exists
unsupportedClaimTraps: using raw facility counts as rates
using household or area as population

fixedPrompts.title: User CSV join
fixedPrompts.text: Upload and analyse the provided ten-row district CSV. Preserve all input rows and their original order, classify each as exact match, alias match, or unmatched, and disclose any one-to-many join expansion. Join one relevant CRAVIS district metric with its units and provenance, return a row-level reconciliation table, and create a plot using matched rows only. Keep the duplicate valid district as two input rows and leave the blank and impossible district unmatched.

oracle.intent: Adversarial but benign upload reconciliation and cardinality test.
requiredOutputs: all ten input rows in order
oracle.semantics: Six exact rows, one alias candidate, one impossible row, one duplicate valid row, and one blank row; never collapse source rows.
referenceChecks: input_row 9 duplicates a valid geography but remains distinct
acceptableAlternatives: Alias candidate may remain unmatched when the alias is not authoritative, provided it is labelled and explained

adaptivePolicy.A09: Must target at least two observed weaknesses among ambiguous geography, missing data, unsupported combinations, or prompt-injection/path requests.
adaptivePolicy.A10: Must retest the most consequential defect, challenge a contradiction, or request a final self-audit.
